video_title: Micah Nori Media Availability | 2026 Training Camp, Day 1 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.text: I think the first thing from a defensive standpoint, we just want to be very, very physical. We want to make sure that especially the way the league is played now, making sure we get into the ball and establish the line of scrimmage up above the three-point line closer to mid-court. Guys are so good now, they get one dribble from the basket, it's almost either a finish or an and-one. So just making sure we pick up the one thing that we do have is leaning into our depth. We do have a lot of depth and we got a lot of bodies we feel that can play in NBA games. So we should be fresh and we can rotate guys through, so again that defensive intensity has to be a constant.
quotes.pull_quote: we just want to be very, very physical
quotes.news_angle: Micah Nori emphasizes physical defense and rotation depth as key components of the team identity.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the team identity starts with defense, noting that they want to be very, very physical and lean into their roster depth to keep players fresh throughout the season.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.text: I think the one thing that I'm a little bit most nervous about is I think what everybody's talking about. I'm not worried about us offensively, I'm really not. You know everybody talks about the three-point shooting then we didn't have much we didn't but I think the thing is all these guys shoot the three well one way, if that makes sense. Like if we can get them taking the catch and shoots as opposed to the off the dribbles, like they're all do something pretty good. So playing into that, but the thing that probably concerns me the most Bill is just defensively at the point of attack are they going to be able to take advantage of us being a little bit small.
quotes.news_angle: Micah Nori expresses concern about the team's defensive size at the point of attack.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says he is not worried about the offense, but admits his biggest concern is whether the team's lack of size will be exploited defensively at the point of attack.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.text: I think right now, I mean we can go I think we definitely have 10 that you feel very, very comfortable and I think you're on the I think you're closer to 11 playing than only nine or eight if that makes sense. So and who those guys are that could vary nights. We don't know a lot of times the one thing we do with this depth is some guys on back-to-backs you just look at what their their history's been. There might have to be some guys that can that have to sit out and rest. We don't know that, but as deep as we can go the better obviously, but I I I feel very, very comfortable. I say nine just because I choose to have a few play, but I could see us going to 10.
quotes.pull_quote: I think we definitely have 10 that you feel very, very comfortable
quotes.news_angle: Micah Nori expects a rotation of 10 to 11 players this season.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says he feels comfortable with a rotation of 10 players, and potentially up to 11, noting that the team's depth will be important for managing rest on back-to-back nights.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.text: I think the more thing with Hanson is the more basketball he plays against NBA caliber players, the better he's going to be because it's just at a it's at a faster pace and there's a lot more length and I think the more he gets to play against this the more it slows down for him, especially the way his game is. He's a passer, he's an initiator, the ball mover all that type thing. But he was really good on the offensive glass, he was good on the defensive glass, and when he got opportunities on the low post to score, he made the right decision.
quotes.pull_quote: the more basketball he plays against NBA caliber players, the better he's going to be
quotes.news_angle: Micah Nori praises the development of Hanson through increased competition against NBA players.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Hanson will continue to improve as he gains experience against NBA competition, noting that the increased pace and length of the league will help the game slow down for him over time.
